Top shows layers 1-2 and bottom shows layers 3-4. 28 8 Conclusions Inthispaper,wepresentanovelmethodologytooptimizethetoolpathtrajectoryofadditivelymanufactured fiber-reinforced composite cylinders comprised of layers of cylindrical annuli. Our DIW process allows us to extrudethermosetresinthroughamovingnozzleandbuildupastructureinnonplanarlayers. Sincethefibers are primarily aligned in the flow direction of the extrudate, the printing trajectory influences the material propertiesofthecompositestructure. ToaccommodateourDIWprocessinourdesignformulation,wedefine the toolpaths as contours of parameterized level-set functions. For convenience, these level-set functions are defined in a planar reference configuration and their contours are mapped to a cylindrical surface. Since arc lengths are the same in both configurations, this mapping allows us to reuse no-overlap and no-sag constraint equations from previous work [25]. To obtain continuous toolpaths, we impose periodicity in our level-setfunctionsandintroduceaninteger level-offsetnumber. Tousegradient-basedoptimization,weadd a design variable and a smooth floor function to approximate the integer level-offset number. We present an algorithm to solve this mixed-integer programming problem via nonlinear programming in a three step process. We illustrate the optimization procedure by solving four design problems. The toolpaths in the optimal designsareplacedandalignedtobestcarrytheloads. Moreover,theseoptimaltoolpathsaremanufacturable astheyarecontinuousandsatisfytheno-sag,no-overlap,andminimumradiusofcurvatureconstraints. The computationalcostoftheoptimizationprocessappearstoberelatedtotheconstraints. Asexpected,designs with active constraints are more computationally expensive to obtain. In future research , we will extend this work for other axisymmetric structures, e.g., cones. As in this work, we plan to represent the toolpaths in a planar reference configuration and then map them to an axisymmetric surface. The major challenge would be to ensure continuity of the toolpaths which might not be straightforward. Additionally, we will study the effectiveness and cost of using other ramp functions to consolidatelocalconstraintsandcompareitwiththeoneproposed.
